written_for: Elena, associate museum exhibition curator and registrar

tasks.title: Audit wheelchair viewing angles and lighting
tasks.prompt: Tell me whether our current gallery hang has any wheelchair viewing angle or paper lighting problems, without moving any artwork.

tasks.title: Dim over-lit woodblock print
tasks.prompt: The Great Wave on the north wall is getting far too much spotlight for a woodblock print on paper. Bring its lighting down within safe conservation limits and leave the other walls untouched.

tasks.title: Lower high frame for seated visitors
tasks.prompt: Lower any painting or print on the north wall that forces a seated wheelchair visitor to tilt their head past twenty-five degrees, and make sure neighboring frames still have at least fifteen centimeters between them.

tasks.title: Full north wall compliance repair
tasks.prompt: Fix every sightline, spacing, placard print size, and lighting violation across the gallery so the exhibition passes all museum standards.

tasks.title: Curate botanical works on north wall
tasks.prompt: Put together a four-work botanical display on the north gallery wall from our Chicago collection, keeping every paper work at fifty lux or below and compliant for seated visitors.

tasks.title: Switch to wheelchair sightline preview on Magnolia
tasks.prompt: Show me the gallery from a seated wheelchair visitor's eye level focused on Redoute's Magnolia Grandiflora, without changing where anything is hung.

tasks.title: Write accessible wall placard and save milestone
tasks.prompt: Write a clear fifty-word museum wall note for Hokusai's Great Wave sized so headset visitors can read it easily from one point two meters, then save a snapshot called Conservation Ready.

tasks.title: Curate architectural study across two walls
tasks.prompt: Arrange Piranesi's architectural etchings and Wright's window elevation across the north and west walls, switch on the tabletop scale model for seated review, and verify zero accessibility or lighting issues.
